subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Tibolone

steps.tx: **Tibolone** is a synthetic 19-nortestosterone steroid derivative classified as a selective tissue estrogenic activity regulator (STEAR), used for managing postmenopausal symptoms. Following oral ingestion, tibolone itself is biologically inert, functioning as a prodrug. In vivo, it is rapidly converted into three active steroid metabolites: 3-alpha-hydroxy-tibolone, 3-beta-hydroxy-tibolone, and the delta-4-isomer. These metabolites display tissue-specific affinities for estrogen, progesterone, and androgen nuclear receptors, conferring distinct organ-selective pharmacological effects.
steps.say: Tibolone is a synthetic steroid that acts as a selective tissue regulator. It breaks down into three metabolites that exert estrogenic, progestogenic, and androgenic actions depending on the specific target organ.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating tissue-selective metabolic actions of tibolone.
vis.caption: Tissue-selective estrogenic, progestogenic, and androgenic actions of tibolone metabolites. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Tissue-selective activity** allows tibolone to provide the clinical benefits of combined hormone replacement therapy within a single molecule. In bone, brain, and the cardiovascular system, the 3-alpha and 3-beta-hydroxy metabolites bind estrogen receptors, preventing osteoclastic bone resorption and suppressing hypothalamic thermoregulatory hot flushes. In the endometrium, the delta-4 isomer acts directly as a potent progestogen and inhibits local sulfatase enzymes, completely preventing estrogenic glandular proliferation and avoiding uterine bleeding.
steps.say: Tibolone acts like estrogen in bone and brain to prevent fractures and hot flushes. But in the uterus, its delta-four metabolite acts as a progestin, stopping the lining from thickening and avoiding bleeding.

vis.title: Target Organ Actions of Tibolone Metabolites
rows: Delta-4 isomer and local sulfatase block
Lowers SHBG, enhances free testosterone and libido

steps.tx: **Endometrial safety** represents a major clinical advantage of tibolone over conventional estrogen-alone therapy in postmenopausal women with an intact uterus. In endometrial stromal and glandular cells, the delta-4 isomer stimulates 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, which converts active estradiol into weaker estrone, while simultaneously inhibiting steroid sulfatase. Consequently, the endometrium remains completely atrophic. Tibolone induces amenorrhoea in over ninety percent of women, eliminating the need for a separate progestin tablet.
steps.say: Tibolone keeps the endometrium atrophic by inhibiting local estrogen production and acting as a progestin. Over ninety percent of women remain completely amenorrhoeic, avoiding annoying withdrawal bleeds.

left.title: Tibolone Endometrial Action
points: Converts local estradiol to weaker estrone

right.title: Conventional Estrogen Alone
points: High hazard of atypical glandular hyperplasia

steps.tx: **Bone mineral density** is preserved and fracture risk reduced by tibolone, as demonstrated in the landmark Long-term Intervention on Fractures with Tibolone (LIFT) trial. Administered at 1.25 or 2.5 milligrams daily, tibolone significantly increases bone density at the lumbar spine and femoral neck, reducing the risk of new vertebral fractures by forty-five percent and non-vertebral fractures by twenty-six percent. It represents an effective second-line therapeutic option for postmenopausal osteopenia and osteoporosis in symptomatic women.
steps.say: Tibolone increases bone mineral density and slashes vertebral fracture risk by forty-five percent. It is an effective option for postmenopausal osteoporosis in women who also suffer from hot flushes.

nodes.label: Osteoblast Binding
nodes.sub: Estrogen receptor alpha activation on bone cells

nodes.label: RANKL Suppression
nodes.sub: Reduces osteoclast recruitment and bone resorption

steps.tx: **Libido and sexual function** improve significantly with tibolone, distinguishing it from conventional hormone replacement regimens. The delta-4 isomer binds directly to androgen receptors in the central nervous system. Furthermore, tibolone moderately suppresses hepatic synthesis of sex hormone-binding globulin, decreasing SHBG levels by up to fifty percent and significantly elevating circulating free, biologically active testosterone. This unique androgenic profile enhances sexual desire, arousal, satisfaction, and psychological mood.
steps.say: Tibolone uniquely improves libido and sexual desire because its androgenic metabolite lowers SHBG, freeing up active testosterone in the bloodstream to boost mood and sexual satisfaction.

vis.title: Androgenic Effects on Sexual Function and Lipid Profile
rows: Superior to conventional HRT for low libido

steps.tx: **Stroke risk** was confirmed as a major adverse safety outcome in the LIFT trial, which was terminated prematurely due to an excess of ischaemic cerebrovascular events. In postmenopausal women aged sixty years and older, tibolone increased the relative risk of ischaemic stroke by 2.2-fold compared to placebo. Consequently, tibolone is strictly contraindicated in women aged sixty and older, those with pre-existing cerebrovascular disease, or individuals with multiple cardiovascular risk factors.
steps.say: The LIFT trial was halted early because tibolone doubled the risk of ischaemic stroke in women aged sixty and older. Never prescribe tibolone to women over sixty or those with stroke risk factors.

left.title: Absolute Contraindications
points: Prior stroke, TIA, or cardiovascular disease
Personal history of breast cancer (LIBERATE trial)

right.title: Appropriate Clinical Candidates
points: At least 12 months since final menses
Bothersome flushes combined with low libido

steps.tx: **Breast cancer recurrence** was documented in the randomized LIBERATE trial evaluating tibolone in postmenopausal breast cancer survivors suffering from vasomotor flushes. The trial was halted prematurely when tibolone demonstrated an unacceptable 1.4-fold increase in the hazard of breast cancer recurrence. Although tibolone exhibits low mammographic breast density in healthy women, a history of breast cancer or any estrogen-sensitive malignancy remains an absolute contraindication to its clinical use.
steps.say: The LIBERATE study showed that tibolone significantly increases the recurrence of breast cancer in survivors. Any personal history of breast cancer is an absolute contraindication to taking tibolone.

nodes.label: Candidate Screening
nodes.sub: Assess personal cancer and stroke history

nodes.label: Absolute Contraindication
nodes.sub: Switch to non-hormonal SSRIs or gabapentin

steps.tx: **Twelve months of amenorrhoea** must elapse before initiating tibolone in women undergoing natural menopause. Because tibolone exerts weak progestogenic activity that cannot overcome high, erratic endogenous estrogen surges characteristic of early perimenopause, starting it too early produces unpredictable, irregular breakthrough vaginal bleeding. Standard adult dosing is 2.5 milligrams orally once daily, swallowed with water at the same time each day without cyclical interruptions.
steps.say: Wait until at least twelve months have passed since the last period before starting tibolone. Prescribing it during early perimenopause causes irregular breakthrough bleeding because erratic natural estrogens override it.

vis.title: Prescribing Rules and Dosing for Tibolone
rows: At least 12 months after last natural menses
Maintains continuous symptom and bone protection
No residual endogenous estrogen surges exist
Balances fracture benefits against stroke risks
